meanings.usage: 常用被动语态be oppressed by表示“被……困扰、压迫”
后常接for sth/doing sth表示“做某事的正当理由”

meanings.meaning: 有正当理由地，无可非议地
meanings.usage: 修饰动词、形容词，说明行为或感受的合理性
可形容人的感受、经历或味道，后常接at/about sth表示“因某事不快”
用于形容行为、处境或状态的糟糕或不光彩

meanings.meaning: 不光彩的，卑劣的（正式用词，与noble（高尚的）语义相反，形容品格或行为）
不受个人情感影响的，客观的
非个人的（前缀im-表否定，对应personal（个人的，主观的））

meanings.usage: 心理学常用术语，也可日常表示“自尊心、自我中心”

meanings.meaning: 后退，退去（主语常为抽象事物（记忆、恐惧）或具体事物（潮水、边界））

meanings.usage: 常用搭配merge into表示“融入……，和……合并”
指体积较大的圆形岩石
可作名词表示衰退状态，也可作动词表示“衰退、腐烂”的动作
不可数名词，形容人或事物的生机活力

meanings.meaning: 疲劳，疲倦（由形容词weary（疲劳的）派生而来，可指身体或精神上的疲惫）

phrases.usage: 表示“被剥夺了……，被骗走了……”，被动结构强调主体失去了本应获得的事物

examples.en: Many children in the poor area are cheated of the right to education.
examples.zh: 贫困地区的很多孩子被剥夺了受教育的权利。

phrases.usage: 副词短语，意为“逐渐地，一点一点地”，等同于gradually，可放在句首或句中修饰动作

examples.en: Bit by bit, he learned how to communicate with others properly.
examples.zh: 他逐渐学会了如何恰当地和他人沟通。

phrases.usage: 表示“融入……，和……融为一体”，也可写作be merged into，强调个体融入更大的整体

examples.en: The small village was gradually merged in the expanding city.
examples.zh: 这个小村庄逐渐被扩张的城市吞并了。

phrases.usage: 表示“遭受……的痛苦，受……困扰”，后常接疾病、负面情绪或不利处境

examples.en: A lot of office workers suffer from neck pain due to long hours of sitting.
examples.zh: 很多上班族因为长时间久坐受到颈椎痛的困扰。

phrases.usage: 表示“想到……”，后接同位语从句说明thought的具体内容，用于描述人的心理活动

examples.en: She smiled in the thought that her family would come to see her soon.
examples.zh: 想到家人很快就要来看她，她露出了微笑。

phrases.usage: 插入语，意为“在我看来，我认为”，用于委婉表达个人观点，可放在句首或句中

examples.en: It seems to me that we should put off the meeting until next week.
examples.zh: 在我看来我们应该把会议推迟到下周。

grammar.title: 定语从句
grammar.structure: 先行词 + 关系代词/副词 + 从句剩余部分
grammar.definition: 修饰名词或代词的从句，用于对先行词进行限定或补充说明，由关系代词或关系副词引导 当先行词是人时常用who/that引导，是物时常用which/that引导，从句用于补充先行词的相关信息

examples.en: Young men who have reason to fear that they will be killed in battle may justifiably feel bitter.
examples.zh: 有理由担心自己会在战场上丧生的年轻人，想到自己被剥夺了生活所能给予的最美好的东西，感到痛苦，这是合乎情理的。

examples.en: The book that you lent me last week is very interesting.
examples.zh: 你上周借给我的那本书非常有趣。

grammar.title: 同位语从句
grammar.structure: 抽象名词 + that + 完整的陈述句
grammar.definition: 在复合句中作名词的同位语的从句，用于说明该名词的具体内容，常跟在fact, thought, idea, hope等抽象名词后 that在同位语从句中不充当成分，只起连接作用，不能省略，用于对前面的抽象名词进行解释说明

examples.en: They were worried over the fact that you were sick.
examples.zh: 他们为你生病的事发愁。

examples.en: I hold the belief that we will finally achieve our goal.
examples.zh: 我坚信我们最终会实现目标。

grammar.title: 方式状语从句
grammar.definition: 用于描述动作的方式、状态的状语从句，常由as, like, as if等词引导 常用于打比方，说明主句动作或状态的特征，as是正式引导词，like多用于口语中

examples.en: An individual human existence should be like a river--small at first, narrowly contained within its banks.
examples.zh: 人的一生应该像一条河——起初很窄，被紧紧地夹在两岸之间。

examples.en: When in Rome, do as the Romans do.

patterns.pattern: Some people are oppressed by the fear of + 名词.

original.en: Some old people are oppressed by the fear of death.
original.zh: 有些老年人因为怕死而感到烦恼。

imitations.en: Many job seekers are oppressed by the fear of unemployment.
imitations.zh: 很多求职者因为害怕失业而感到压抑。

imitations.en: Some students are oppressed by the fear of failure in exams.
imitations.zh: 有些学生因为害怕考试不及格而倍感压力。

patterns.pattern: The best way to overcome it is to + 动词短语, until + 结果状语从句.

original.en: The best way to overcome it--so at least it seems to me--is to make your interests gradually wider and more impersonal, until bit by bit the walls of the ego recede, and your life becomes increasingly merged in the universal life.
original.zh: 克服怕死的最好办法——至少在我看来是这样——就是逐渐使自己的兴趣更加广泛，逐渐摆脱个人狭小的圈子，直到自我的屏障慢慢消失，你的生活越来越融入整个社会生活之中。

imitations.en: The best way to overcome stage fright is to practice speaking in public more often, until you can express your ideas fluently in front of crowds.
imitations.zh: 克服怯场的最好办法就是多练习公开发言，直到你能在人群面前流利地表达自己的想法。

imitations.en: The best way to overcome language barriers is to immerse yourself in the language environment, until you can communicate with native speakers without difficulty.
imitations.zh: 克服语言障碍的最好办法就是把自己沉浸在语言环境中，直到你能毫不费力地和母语者交流。

patterns.pattern: The man who, in + 场景, can see his life in this way, will not suffer from + 负面事物.

original.en: The man who, in old age can see his life in this way, will not suffer from the fear of death, since the things he cares for will continue.
original.zh: 人到老年如果这样看待人生，就不会因为怕死而感到痛苦，因为他所关心的事情还会继续下去。

imitations.en: The man who, in face of setbacks, can see his life in this way, will not suffer from self-doubt, since he knows failure is a necessary part of growth.
imitations.zh: 面对挫折时如果这样看待人生的人，就不会陷入自我怀疑，因为他知道失败是成长的必经部分。

imitations.en: The student who, in the face of heavy study tasks, can see his efforts in this way, will not suffer from anxiety, since he knows every bit of effort pays off.
imitations.zh: 面对繁重的学习任务时如果这样看待自己的付出的学生，就不会饱受焦虑的困扰，因为他知道每一点努力都有回报。

lines.en: Some old people are oppressed by the fear of death.
lines.zh: 有些老年人因为怕死而感到烦恼。

lines.en: In the young there is a justification for this feeling.
lines.zh: 青年人有这种感觉是情有可原的。

lines.en: Young men who have reason to fear that they will be killed in battle may justifiably feel bitter in the thought that they have cheated of the best things that life has to offer.
lines.zh: 有理由害怕自己会死在战场上的年轻人，想到自己被剥夺了生活所能给予的最美好的东西时，感到痛苦，这是可以理解的。

lines.en: But in an old man who has known human joys and sorrows, and has achieved whatever work it was in him to do, the fear of death is somewhat abject and ignoble .
lines.zh: 可是老年人已经饱尝了人间的甘苦，一切能做的都做了，如果怕死，就有点儿可怜又可鄙。

lines.en: The best way to overcome it -- so at least it seems to me -- is to make your interests gradually wider and more impersonal , until bit by bit the walls of the ego recede , and your life becomes increasingly merged in the universal life.
lines.zh: 克服怕死的最好办法--至少在我看来是这样--就是逐渐使自己的兴趣更加广泛，逐渐摆脱个人狭小的圈子，直到自我的围墙一点一点地倒塌下来，自己的生活慢慢地和整个宇宙的生活融合在一起。

lines.en: An individual human existence should be like a river -- small at first, narrowly contained within its banks, and rushing passionately past boulders and over waterfalls.
lines.zh: 个人的存在应该像一条河流，开始很小，被紧紧地夹在两岸中间，接着热情奔放地冲过巨石，飞下瀑布。

lines.en: Gradually the river grows wider, the banks recede, the waters flow more quietly, and in the end, without any visible break, they become merged in the sea, and painlessly lose their individual being.
lines.zh: 然后河面渐渐地变宽，两岸后撤，河水流得平缓起来，最后连绵不断地汇入大海，毫无痛苦地失去了自我的存在。

lines.en: The man who, in old age, can see his life in this way, will not suffer from the fear of death, since the things he cares for will continue. And if, with the decay of vitality , weariness increases, the thought of rest will be not unwelcome.
lines.zh: 上了年纪的人这样看待生命，就不会有惧怕死亡的心情了，因为自己关心的一切事件都会继续下去。

lines.en: I should wish to die while still at work, knowing that others will carry on what I can no longer do, and content in the thought that what was possible has been done. BERTRAND RUSSELL How to grow old from Portraits from Memory
lines.zh: 再者，随着精力的衰退，老年人的疲惫会增长，有长眠的愿望未尝不是一件好事情，我希望工作到死为止，明白了有人会继续我的未竟事业，想到能做的事都做了，也就坦然了。

questions.q: What, according to the author, is the best way to overcome the fear of death as you get older?
questions.zh: 按照作者的说法，人上了年纪后，克服对死亡的恐惧的最好办法是什么？
questions.a: To make your interests gradually wider and more impersonal, until bit by bit the walls of the ego recede and your life becomes increasingly merged in the universal life.
questions.aZh: 逐渐使自己的兴趣更加广泛、更加忘我，直到自我的围墙一点点退去，生命渐渐融入整个宇宙的生命。
questions.hint: 见课文第五句 The best way to overcome it ... is to make your interests gradually wider and more impersonal...

questions.q: Why does the author say the fear of death is justifiable in the young?
questions.zh: 作者为什么说青年人对死亡的恐惧是情有可原的？
questions.a: Because young men who have reason to fear that they will be killed in battle may justifiably feel bitter in the thought that they have been cheated of the best things life has to offer.
questions.aZh: 因为有理由担心自己会战死沙场的年轻人，一想到自己被剥夺了生活所能给予的最美好的东西，感到痛苦是理所应当的。
questions.hint: 见课文第二、三句 the young / killed in battle / cheated of the best things...

questions.q: What simile does the author use to describe an individual human existence, and how does it change?
questions.zh: 作者用什么比喻来形容个人的存在？这一比喻又如何变化？
questions.a: He compares it to a river: small at first and narrowly contained within its banks, rushing passionately past boulders and over waterfalls, then growing wider and flowing more quietly, until at last it merges painlessly in the sea.
questions.aZh: 他把个人存在比作河流：起初很小、被紧紧夹在两岸之间，热情奔放地冲过巨石、飞下瀑布，然后河面渐宽、水流渐缓，最后毫无痛苦地汇入大海。
questions.hint: 见课文第六、七句 like a river / grows wider / merged in the sea...

questions.q: How does the author wish to die, and why is the thought of rest not unwelcome?
questions.zh: 作者希望怎样死去？他为什么说长眠之念“未尝不是一件好事情”？
questions.a: He would wish to die while still at work, knowing that others will carry on what he can no longer do and content that what was possible has been done; as vitality decays and weariness increases, the thought of rest is not unwelcome.
questions.aZh: 他希望工作到死为止，因为知道有人会继续他未竟的事业，想到能做的都做了也就坦然；随着精力衰退、倦意增长，长眠之念也就不再令人反感。
questions.hint: 见课文第八、九句 the decay of vitality / I should wish to die while still at work...

questions.q: The author calls the fear of death in a fulfilled old man 'abject and ignoble'. Do you agree that widening one's impersonal interests can overcome it? Give your reasons.
questions.zh: 作者认为，饱经沧桑、功成事毕的老人若仍怕死就“可怜又可鄙”。你同意“让兴趣日益广泛忘我”能克服这种恐惧吗？请说明理由。
questions.a: Open-ended. A possible answer: Yes. When one's interests reach beyond the self, one's life merges with what will continue after death — in science, art, or the welfare of others — so personal extinction loses its terror; one dies content that the work goes on.
questions.aZh: 开放性作答。参考：同意。当兴趣超越小我，生命便融入死后仍将延续的事业（科学、艺术或他人的福祉），个人的消亡不再可怕，人也就能坦然工作到死。
questions.hint: 结合课文第五、八、九句作答，言之成理即可。

translation:
有些老年人因为怕死而感到烦恼。
青年人有这种感觉是情有可原的。
有理由害怕自己会死在战场上的年轻人，想到自己被剥夺了生活所能给予的最美好的东西时，感到痛苦，这是可以理解的。
可是老年人已经饱尝了人间的甘苦，一切能做的都做了，如果怕死，就有点儿可怜又可鄙。
克服怕死的最好办法--至少在我看来是这样--就是逐渐使自己的兴趣更加广泛，逐渐摆脱个人狭小的圈子，直到自我的围墙一点一点地倒塌下来，自己的生活慢慢地和整个宇宙的生活融合在一起。
个人的存在应该像一条河流，开始很小，被紧紧地夹在两岸中间，接着热情奔放地冲过巨石，飞下瀑布。
然后河面渐渐地变宽，两岸后撤，河水流得平缓起来，最后连绵不断地汇入大海，毫无痛苦地失去了自我的存在。
上了年纪的人这样看待生命，就不会有惧怕死亡的心情了，因为自己关心的一切事件都会继续下去。
再者，随着精力的衰退，老年人的疲惫会增长，有长眠的愿望未尝不是一件好事情，我希望工作到死为止，明白了有人会继续我的未竟事业，想到能做的事都做了，也就坦然了。
title: How to Grow Old
subtitle: 如何安度晚年

lead.question: 人终将老去，如何才能不惧死亡、安然度过晚年？哲学家罗素给出的答案是什么？
lead.warmup: 伯特兰·罗素是英国哲学家、数学家。这篇随笔写于他年近八旬之时，语调平和而豁达。作者从老年人对死亡的恐惧谈起，提出把个人兴趣逐渐向外扩展、忘掉小我，像河流汇入大海一样融入更广阔的生命。文章比喻生动，说理从容，是英语散文中的名篇。读时注意它层层递进的逻辑与凝练的用词。
goals: 理解“逐渐扩大兴趣、超越小我”这一核心观点及其河流比喻
掌握 oppressed by、impersonal、abject and ignoble、the decay of vitality 等表达
学会用定语从句和 since 引导的原因从句组织复合句
体会英语议论散文说理从容、比喻贴切的文体特点
lead.summary: 有些老年人因怕死而烦恼，但饱经甘苦、功成事毕的老人若仍怕死，就显得可怜可鄙。罗素认为，最好的办法是让兴趣日益广泛忘我，使自我之墙渐渐退去，生命融入宇宙的生命。个人存在如河流，由窄而宽，最终无声汇入大海。这样看待一生的人不会惧死；他愿工作到死，因为事业有人接续。
lead.tips: 易错：the best way to overcome it 中 to overcome 是不定式作定语，别写成 overcoming；主语 The best way 是单数，谓语用 is 而非 are。

exercises.q: 汉译英：有些老年人因怕死而感到烦恼。
exercises.a: Some old people are oppressed by the fear of death.

exercises.q: 汉译英：老年人的怕死有点可怜又可鄙。
exercises.a: The fear of death in an old man is somewhat abject and ignoble.

exercises.q: 用括号中词的适当形式填空：The best way ___ (overcome) it is to make your interests more ___ (impersonal).
exercises.note: 不定式作定语，impersonal 作表语

exercises.q: 句型转换：将两句合并为含定语从句的复合句。Young men may feel bitter. / They have reason to fear that they will be killed in battle.
exercises.a: Young men who have reason to fear that they will be killed in battle may feel bitter.

exercises.q: 改错：The best way to overcome it are to make your interests wider.
exercises.note: 主语 the best way 为单数

exercises.q: 句型转换：用 since 把后句改写为原因状语从句。He will not suffer from the fear of death. / The things he cares for will continue.
exercises.a: He will not suffer from the fear of death, since the things he cares for will continue.
exercises.note: since 引导原因状语从句

exercises.q: 改错：Others will carry on that I can no longer do.

quiz.q: 作者认为克服对死亡恐惧的最好办法是什么？
options: To make your interests gradually wider and more impersonal.
To live a quiet life alone by a river.
To think about death as little as possible.
To leave all your work to others.

quiz.q: 作者为什么认为年轻人的怕死情有可原？
options: Because young men are naturally afraid of pain.
Because young men have known few joys and sorrows.
Because young men may be killed in battle and be cheated of life's best things.
Because young men have done nothing worthwhile.
quiz.note: 见第三句 killed in battle

quiz.q: 作者把个人的存在比作什么？
options: A waterfall.
A river.
A boulder.
The sea.
quiz.note: like a river 是中心比喻

quiz.q: 作者用 abject and ignoble 形容什么？
options: The death of a soldier in battle.
The weariness of old age.
The interests of young people.
The fear of death in an old man who has known joys and sorrows.
quiz.note: 见第四句 in an old man

quiz.q: 作者希望自己怎样死去？
options: While still at work, knowing that others will carry on what he can no longer do.
Peacefully in his sleep at home.
Far away from his family and friends.
Long before his vitality decays.
quiz.note: 见末句 die while still at work

quiz.q: the walls of the ego recede 意思最接近？
options: The walls of the house fall down.
One becomes more self-centred.
One loses all interest in life.
The sense of self gradually gives way.
quiz.note: ego 指自我，recede 指退去
